chain.label: Significant vertical wind shear and convective activity aloft near a low pressure area
chain.trigger: Significant vertical windshears were evident from approximately 33,000 feet to about 40,000 feet

chain.label: MD-11 relaxed longitudinal stability produces very light control column forces in high-altitude cruise
chain.trigger: the probable cause of this incident was the light control force characteristics of the MD-11 airplane in high altitude cruise flight

chain.label: No DAC or China Airlines training for recovery from high-altitude, high-speed upsets
chain.trigger: there were no specific training procedures in either the MD-11 training or flight manuals at DAC or at China Airlines that addressed recognizing and dealing with abrupt pitch variations

chain.label: Reduced bead-to-skin adhesive bond strength in the composite elevators (local lack of sanding, elevated void content)
chain.trigger: the dull, matte surface was covered with somewhat intact peel ply imprints indicating a local lack of sanding... The China Airlines elevator lap shear specimen strength was significantly lower than similar specimens from the Korean Airlines elevator assembly

chain.label: Airplane encountered moderate turbulence in cruise at FL330
chain.trigger: encountered moderate turbulence at flight level 330

caused_by.evidence: Calculated values for vertical and horizontal windshears were conducive to turbulence of at least moderate intensity

chain.label: Moderate lateral gust from the left produced sideslip and a rapid roll to 30 degrees right wing down
chain.trigger: At the start of the upset, a 0.25 G lateral acceleration to the right was recorded... This excursion is consistent with a gust from the left side of the airplane

caused_by.evidence: flight CI-012 encountered moderate turbulence that preceded the violent motions of the airplane

chain.label: Autopilot and autothrottles disconnected, leaving the pilot in manual control
chain.trigger: The autopilot was disconnected at the start of the roll excursion

caused_by.evidence: The autopilot disconnected, probably from excessive roll rate

chain.label: Pilot mistook self-induced stall buffet for severe turbulence and disregarded the stall warning
chain.trigger: he did not recognize that the motion cues were the result of stall buffet that he induced

caused_by.evidence: That training should be comprehensive enough so that pilots can differentiate between severe turbulence and stall buffet
Since the pilot stated that he was experiencing severe turbulence

chain.label: Pilot commanded excessive wheel and control column deflections during upset and recovery
chain.trigger: Aileron and elevator control deflections commanded by the pilot resulted in excessive roll and pitch excursions, at least four aerodynamic stalls, and almost continuous stall warning activation

caused_by.evidence: The initial overcontrol was the result of the light control forces inherent in the MD-11 design
Contributing to the incident was a lack of pilot training specific to the recovery from high altitude, high speed upsets in the MD-11
the pilot applied LWD wheel deflection to counteract the increasing right roll angle
If the autopilot is disconnected while the pilot is exerting force on the control column... an abrupt change in the elevator position will be induced by the pilot
the pilot chose to ignore the stall warning system and had to override the 50-pound control column force

chain.label: Airplane pitched up to 23 degrees ANU and zoomed to 35,800 feet with airspeed decaying to 160 KIAS
chain.trigger: The altitude increased from 33,000 feet to about 35,800 feet, and the indicated airspeed decreased from about 290 KIAS to 160 KIAS

caused_by.evidence: The control column deflections resulted in rapidly increasing AOA and pitch angles... The airplane transitioned into a 7,000 feet-per-minute climb for the next 30 seconds and slowed to the 1 G stall speed

chain.label: Pilot applied nose-up trim during the high-altitude recovery contrary to manufacturer guidance
chain.trigger: Although DAC recommends that the airplane not be retrimmed following a high altitude, high speed loss of control, the pilot applied ANU trim during the climb

caused_by.evidence: neither DAC nor China Airlines had addressed the issue of high altitude upsets in their training or flight manuals
the pilot applied ANU trim during the climb

chain.label: Airplane stalled and pitched down at least four times during the recovery
chain.trigger: Similar excursions at 66, 104, and 118 seconds indicated that the airplane stalled and pitched down at least four times during the recovery

caused_by.evidence: the pilot continued to use excessive elevator deflection that resulted in excursions between 0.6 G and 1.6 G
the airplane... slowed to the 1 G stall speed

the continuing pitch up motion when the elevator was returned to neutral was a direct result of the pilot retrimming the airplane... The continued increase in pitch and AOA contributed to the first stall break

chain.label: Airplane departed controlled flight for about three minutes of pitch and roll excursions
chain.trigger: The airplane subsequently departed controlled flight

caused_by.evidence: how the turbulence and pilot reactions resulted in the loss of control of the airplane
almost continuous stall warning activation for a period of about 2 minutes and 45 seconds

chain.label: Stall buffet excited the outboard elevator torsion mode, loading the elevators above design limit load
chain.trigger: the outboard elevator horn balance weights being excited in the 10.5 HZ elevator torsion mode which twisted the outboard elevators

caused_by.evidence: the separation of the elevator skin most likely occurred during the stall buffet when the elevators were loaded above the design limit load
In the 89.75 seconds in which CI-012 exceeded the buffet boundary, the airplane was more than 20 percent above the buffet boundary for 27.1 seconds

chain.label: Left and right outboard elevator skins fractured and disbonded, with sections separating from the airplane
chain.trigger: sustained damage to the left and right outboard elevator skin assemblies, portions of which separated from the airplane

caused_by.evidence: the elevator buffet damage in the five MD-11 airplane incidents was caused by overstress
Examination of the three samples with the SEM revealed a predominantly adhesive mode of failure between the adhesive and the bonded structure

chain.label: Control regained about three minutes after the upset; flight continued and landed uneventfully at Anchorage
chain.trigger: Airplane control was established about 3 minutes after the initial upset when the elevators were returned to neutral and the speed increased to above 200 KIAS

caused_by.evidence: The airplane continued on and landed uneventfully at Anchorage, Alaska
